predecessors.name: County of Urgell
predecessors.text: Cerdanya (with Conflent and Berga), which Wilfred the Hairy held with Urgell from 870 until his death in 897

successors.name: Crown of Aragon
successors.text: Cerdanya and Roussillon, which reverted to the Crown of Aragon when Nuño Sánchez died in 1242

rulers.name: Peter (Pere, son of Ramon Berenguer IV)

ledger.x: 897: Wilfred the Hairy dies and his son Miró II receives Cerdanya and Berga.
912: Miró II takes Besalú as well and the two counties are drawn together until 927.
927: Miró II dies and his territories are divided among his four sons; Besalú goes to Wilfred II.
957: after a revolt at Besalú Sunifred II of Cerdanya takes over the county, which is held with Cerdanya-Berga until 988.
988: Oliba Cabreta enters Montecassino and divides his lands; Besalú goes to Bernard Tallaferro.
988: Vallespir, Fenouillèdes and Peyrepertuse go with Besalú to Bernard Tallaferro.
1002: Berga, which had its own counts from 988, is annexed to Cerdanya and the one row goes on as Cerdanya.
1111: Vallespir, Fenolledès, Peyrepertuse and Castellnou come to Cerdanya as compensation for Barcelona's inheritance of Besalú.
1117: Cerdanya passes to Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona.
1162: Cerdanya passes from Barcelona to Peter, a younger son of Ramon Berenguer IV, and is a county of its own again.
1168: Sancho I succeeds as count of Cerdanya.
1199: Berga is sold to King Peter II of Aragon.
About 1209: Peter II of Aragon grants Roussillon to his uncle Sancho, who now holds Cerdanya and Roussillon together.
1242: Nuño Sánchez dies and Cerdanya and Roussillon revert to the Crown of Aragon.
1242: the appanage of Cerdanya and Roussillon ends and its land goes to the Crown of Aragon.

wars.name: Revolt of 957 in Besalú
wars.outcome: Wilfred (II) of Besalú was assassinated and Sunifred of Cerdanya took over the county; Besalú is drawn as a dependent of the Cerdanya counts until 988.

wars.name: Dispute over the inheritance of Besalú (1111)
wars.outcome: Bernard William of Cerdanya, Besalú's feudal suzerain, received four trans-Pyrenean districts as compensation when Barcelona inherited Besalú.

certainty.note: Comital frontiers follow pagi and castles; no page gives a treaty or survey line.
